title: Isometric rigidity of minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphisms between closed spherical cone surfaces with arbitrary positive cone angles
source_title: Rigidity of minimal Lagrangian diffeomorphisms between spherical cone surfaces
author: Christian El Emam; Andrea Seppi
difficulty_reason: The usual maximum principle cannot be applied across cone points before the new metric is proved to have punctured-disc conformal type. Section4 constructs equivariant Euclidean immersions from the Codazzi data, controls their cone-point limits and projects to a flat metric to rule out annulus conformal type despite only continuous extension. This nonroutine local argument closes the global rigidity proof in Section3 without imposing extra cone-angle assumptions.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem1.1 for closed spherical cone surfaces and a smooth regular-locus diffeomorphism extending to a homeomorphism mapping cone points to cone points, with the positive self-adjoint unit-determinant Codazzi tensor of Definition2.2. Cone angles have no upper bound and no additional matching-angle/quasiconformal regularity hypothesis is assumed. Complete new conformal-type proof11–15, Codazzi curvature/eigenvalue maximum-principle argument6–11 and AppendixA equivalence17–19 read. Existing Codazzi Hessian-potential theorem, fundamental theorem of surfaces, uniformization/quasiconformal invariance and Schwarz reflection are explicit research/classical foundations. Original13 equivariance display prints sigma instead of varsigma on the right; the immediately established varsigma=(sigma+dev)/2 and respective holonomies give the same authored construction. Flat projection inequalities apply to quadratic values(v,v), not arbitrary bilinear pairs as one display abbreviates. No independent matched-angle local regularity remark, detailed cone-angle strengthening Remark4.3 or branched-immersion corollary counted separately; no extension to open surfaces.
